title: A height-one normalization prime contracts to an associated prime of a principal quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where an integral domain is a nonzero commutative ring without zero divisors. Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ be its field of fractions and $N\subseteq K$ its integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. If $Q\subset N$ has height one and $a\in R$ satisfies $0\ne a\in Q\cap R$, then $q=Q\cap R$ is an associated prime of $R/aR$: there exists a nonzero class $\bar z\in R/aR$ with $q=\{r\in R:r\bar z=0\}$. Here a height-one prime is a nonzero prime with no prime strictly between it and $(0)$.

source.place: Swanson–Huneke, Integral Closure of Ideals, Rings, and Modules. Lemma 4.9.5, printed pp. 88-89 (PDF pp. 102-103), and its use in the first domain paragraph of Theorem 4.10.5, printed p. 90: depth R_q=1 makes q associated to R/aR for nonzero a in q. Author-hosted PDF read online at https://www.math.purdue.edu/~iswanso/book/SwansonHuneke.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Set $S=R\setminus q$, $A=R_q\subset K$, and $\mathfrak m=qA$. Contraction of a prime is prime, so these localizations are defined. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], $A$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], $B=S^{-1}N\subset K$ is the integral closure of $A$ in $K$; indeed $S^{-1}K=K$ since $S$ consists of nonzero elements. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], $Q'=QB$ is prime and contracts to $Q$ in $N$ and to $\mathfrak m$ in $A$. Every prime below $Q$ is disjoint from $S$, so prime correspondence preserves all chains below $Q$; hence $Q'$ has height one. The element $a$ remains nonzero and lies in $\mathfrak m$. We first prove $\operatorname{depth}A=1$.

source.place: Swanson–Huneke Lemma 4.9.5, printed pp. 88–89 (PDF pages 102–103, 1-based), and the associated-prime application in Theorem 4.10.5, printed p. 90. Author-hosted PDF read at https://www.math.purdue.edu/~iswanso/book/SwansonHuneke.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-normalization-finite-local-model] to the Noetherian domain $A$, its fraction field $K$, its integral closure $B$, and $Q'$. Obtain $A\subseteq C\subseteq B$ generated by finitely many elements over $A$, with $P=Q'\cap C$ and $\dim C_P=1$. In particular $P\cap A=\mathfrak m$, so $a\in P$ and $P\ne(0)$. The prime $P$ has height one: prime correspondence for $C\to C_P$ identifies its prime chains below $P$ with those in the one-dimensional local domain $C_P$.

source.place: Swanson–Huneke Lemma 4.9.5, printed pp. 88–89 (PDF pages 102–103, 1-based), and the associated-prime application in Theorem 4.10.5, printed p. 90. Author-hosted PDF read at https://www.math.purdue.edu/~iswanso/book/SwansonHuneke.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Write $C=A[c_1,\ldots,c_t]$. Each $c_i\in B$ satisfies a monic equation over $A$ of degree $e_i\ge1$, by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Reducing powers with these equations shows that the finitely many monomials $c_1^{j_1}\cdots c_t^{j_t}$, $0\le j_i<e_i$, span $C$ as an $A$-module (for $t=0$, use $1$). Write these monomials as fractions in $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and let $d\ne0$ be the product of their denominators. Then $dC\subseteq A$. Put $x=ad$. Thus $0\ne x\in\mathfrak m$ and $xC\subseteq A$. This constructs the required conductor element; no finiteness of $B$ is assumed.

proof.text: Multiplication by $x$ on the domain $A$ is injective, so [lem-weil-pbc-depth-drops-by-one], with the nonzero cyclic finite module $M=A$, gives a finite integer $h=\operatorname{depth}A\ge1$ and $\operatorname{depth}(A/xA)=h-1$. Suppose $h\ge2$. The module $A/xA$ is cyclic, and $\mathfrak m(A/xA)\ne A/xA$ because its quotient is $A/\mathfrak m\ne0$. By [def-weil-pbc-depth] and [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], depth at least one supplies a regular sequence of positive length in $\mathfrak m$ on $A/xA$. Let $y\in\mathfrak m$ be its first element. Multiplication by $y$, and therefore by every positive power $y^n$, is injective on $A/xA$.

source.place: Swanson–Huneke Lemma 4.9.5, printed pp. 88–89 (PDF pages 102–103, 1-based), and the associated-prime application in Theorem 4.10.5, printed p. 90. Author-hosted PDF read at https://www.math.purdue.edu/~iswanso/book/SwansonHuneke.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Since $0\ne x\in P$ and $P$ has height one in the domain $C$, $P$ is minimal among primes containing $xC$: a smaller such prime would be a nonzero prime strictly between $(0)$ and $P$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-localization-radical] to $C$, $I=xC$, and $P$. Its conclusion is $\sqrt{xC_P}=PC_P$. As $y\in\mathfrak m\subset P$, there is $n\ge1$ with $y^n/1\in xC_P$. Thus $y^n/1=xc/b$ for some $c\in C$ and $b\in C\setminus P$. The fraction equality gives $by^n=xc$ in $C$, because $C\subset K$ is a domain. In particular $by^n\in xC$.

proof.text: Now $by^n=xc$ has $b\in A^\times$ and $c\in C=A$, so $y^n\in xA$. Multiplication by $y^n$ on $A/xA$ kills the class of $1$, and it is injective by Step 4. Consequently $1\in xA$, contradicting $x\in\mathfrak m$. This excludes $h\ge2$; together with $h\ge1$ it proves $\operatorname{depth}A=1$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-depth-drops-by-one] again, now to $M=A$ and the original $0\ne a\in\mathfrak m$. All hypotheses hold: $A$ is Noetherian and local, $A$ is a nonzero cyclic finite module, and a nonzero element acts injectively on a domain. It follows that $A/aA\ne0$ and $\operatorname{depth}(A/aA)=0$.

source.place: Swanson–Huneke Lemma 4.9.5, printed pp. 88–89 (PDF pages 102–103, 1-based), and the associated-prime application in Theorem 4.10.5, printed p. 90. Author-hosted PDF read at https://www.math.purdue.edu/~iswanso/book/SwansonHuneke.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: If $\mathfrak m$ were not associated to the finite cyclic $A$-module $A/aA$, [lem-weil-pbc-nonzerodivisor-if-maximal-not-associated] would give $t\in\mathfrak m$ acting injectively on $A/aA$. But $A/(a,t)A\ne0$, since $(a,t)A\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Thus $t$ would be a regular sequence of length one on $A/aA$ by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], contradicting depth zero by [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Hence there is $w\in A/aA$ with annihilator $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Swanson–Huneke Lemma 4.9.5, printed pp. 88–89 (PDF pages 102–103, 1-based), and the associated-prime application in Theorem 4.10.5, printed p. 90. Author-hosted PDF read at https://www.math.purdue.edu/~iswanso/book/SwansonHuneke.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Identify $(R/aR)_q$ with $A/aA$ by $\bar r/s\mapsto r/s\bmod aA$. This is surjective since every element of $A$ is a fraction $r/s$. Its kernel is zero: $r/s\in aA$ means $r/s=av/t$ with $t\notin q$, so $tr=asv$ in the domain $R$; hence $t\bar r=0$, which is exactly localized vanishing by [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The converse follows by the same equation. This identification is $A$-linear, so the witness in Step 9 has annihilator $qA$ in $(R/aR)_q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-associated-prime-from-localization] to $R$, $M=R/aR$, and the prime $q$; $R$ is Noetherian as required. Obtain a class $\bar z$ with annihilator $q$. Since $q$ is proper, $\bar z\ne0$ (the zero class has annihilator $R$). This proves every clause of the item.
